key_insight: SpatialBench reveals that current spatial foundation models are not yet 'all-round' — many struggle to generalize consistently across tasks, viewpoints, scene domains, input densities, and hardware constraints.
problem_solved: Fills the gap of fragmented evaluations by providing a unified, holistic benchmark to assess generalization and robustness of spatial foundation models across multiple realistic axes of variation.
method: Construct a comprehensive benchmark suite (SpatialBench) that spans multiple downstream tasks and stress axes: viewpoint changes, domain shifts, input density variation, and hardware/runtime constraints.
Curate diverse datasets and controlled perturbations plus standardized robustness and efficiency metrics to enable apples-to-apples comparisons.
Perform large-scale evaluations of popular spatial foundation models and analyze failure modes, trade-offs, and practical deployment limits.
impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to reliably compare models for real-world spatial applications, guiding model selection, architecture improvements, and targeted dataset collection to close robustness gaps.
visual_elements: Radar chart comparing multiple models across robustness axes (viewpoint, domain, density, efficiency).
Heatmap/matrix of model performance per downstream task × domain, highlighting consistent failures.
Before/after example panels showing model outputs under viewpoint shifts and density changes.
Scatter plot of accuracy vs. runtime/hardware cost to visualize deployment trade-offs.
paper_title: SpatialBench: Is Your Spatial Foundation Model an All-Round Player?
paper_authors: Haosong Peng, Hao Li, Jiaqi Chen, Yuhao Pan, Runmao Yao
